headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API/browser egress plus shared file/log surfaces create leakage and cascading-action risk when paired with Opik’s observability outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Opik can expose or render evaluation content, and RD-Agent can ingest browser/API-derived material; if Opik outputs are copied into RD-Agent workflows, prompt-like content could steer downstream behavior. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than direct. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are pasted into RD-Agent prompts or task files
IF RD-Agent treats copied evaluation text as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy: strip instructions from Opik outputs before reuse.
Add a one-line delimiter header when transferring text between tools.
Review any shared workspace files before RD-Agent reads them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce prompt/content separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches logs, execution traces, and financial/research datasets and sends data to external APIs; Opik has broad network egress and REST API access, so pairing them can move sensitive work products across service boundaries. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, but the documented egress and data classes make leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF RD-Agent processes logs or execution traces containing sensitive content
IF Opik forwards those artifacts through its REST API or other network egress
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields before sending artifacts to either agent.
Disable external API calls for nonessential runs.
Separate workspaces so Opik outputs are not stored beside RD-Agent logs.
Rotate any API keys used by RD-Agent after sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Opik only shows REST API egress, while RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs; there is no documented shared mutable directory or overlapping write target. The main conflict is operational contention if both are pointed at the same workspace, which is unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF RD-Agent instances share the same log path without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories for each agent.
Run only one writer per workspace at a time.
Check for duplicate log filenames before execution.
Use per-run subfolders for RD-Agent logs.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is an automation/research system that can act on generated outputs, while Opik produces evaluation/observability artifacts that may be treated as authoritative. If Opik-derived summaries are fed into RD-Agent without verification, errors can cascade into downstream research or API actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are used as inputs to RD-Agent decision steps
IF RD-Agent executes actions without an independent verification stage
mitigations: Require a human review step before RD-Agent acts on Opik outputs.
Compare Opik summaries against raw source artifacts.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only runs when consuming Opik results.
Tag generated summaries as non-authoritative.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple third-party API keys, while Opik is an observability/evaluation tool with broad egress. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, residency, and third-party processing for sensitive research or financial data. Opik is the less clearly governed side, so both profiles matter, but the mismatch is inferred from docs-only evidence.
conditions: IF financial reports or regulated datasets are routed through Opik
IF retention or residency requirements apply to RD-Agent logs or traces
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent.
Keep regulated datasets out of external API paths.
Document retention periods for logs and traces.
Confirm vendor terms for any third-party processing.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
